what: The Pregnancy Due Date Calculator estimates when your baby is due and shows how far along you are today. It works from the first day of your last period, a known conception date, an IVF embryo transfer, or the pregnancy age measured on an ultrasound scan.

Along with the due date it shows your current week and day, your trimester, how many days are left, the likely time of conception, and the dates of common scans, tests and milestones, so you can plan ahead.

It is an estimate and not medical advice. Your doctor or midwife sets your official due date, often after an early scan. Everything is calculated in your browser and the dates you enter are not saved.
uses: Just found out you are pregnant
Enter the first day of your last period to see your due date and how many weeks pregnant you are.
Set your usual cycle length from 20 to 45 days to adjust the estimate.
Use the transfer date and embryo age (day 3 or day 5) for the most precise date.
Enter the scan date and the weeks and days shown on the report to match your clinic's dating.
See when the anatomy scan, glucose test and full term fall, and copy the list for your calendar.
tutorial: In "Calculate from" pick First day of last period, Conception date, IVF embryo transfer or Ultrasound scan. The boxes below change to match.
Enter the first day of your last period, not the last day. If your cycle is usually longer or shorter than 28 days, enter its length; the due date moves by the difference.

For a known conception date, the due date is 266 days later. For IVF, enter the transfer date and choose the embryo age; a day 5 embryo gives a due date 261 days after transfer, a day 3 embryo 263 days.
Enter the date of the scan and the pregnancy age it showed, for example 12 weeks 3 days. The calculator counts back to the start of the pregnancy and adds 280 days.
The due date is shown at the top with the rule used. Below are your weeks and days pregnant today, the trimester, days to go, and the likely conception date or fertile window.
The table lists key weeks such as the dating scan, NIPT, nuchal scan, anatomy scan, glucose test and full term, with their dates. Past milestones are greyed out and the current one is marked.
Click Copy summary to copy the due date and milestone dates into a note, message or calendar.
features: Last period, conception date, IVF transfer (day 3, 5 or 6) and ultrasound dating.
Naegele's rule adjusted for cycles from 20 to 45 days.
See exactly how far along you are today, counted the way doctors do.
Shows the likely fertile window and ovulation date, or the exact conception or fertilisation date when known.
Dates for common scans, tests and pregnancy stages, worked out from your dates.
Nothing you enter is stored or sent anywhere.

example.title: Worked example: a 35-day cycle
example.text: Your last period started on 1 August 2026 and your cycles are usually 35 days. A 28-day cycle would give 1 August + 280 days = 8 May 2027. Because your cycle is 7 days longer, ovulation probably happened about 7 days later, so the calculator adds 7 days: the estimated due date is Saturday 15 May 2027. On 20 November 2026 you would be 14 weeks 6 days pregnant, in the 2nd trimester, with 176 days to go. Ovulation was most likely around 22 August 2026, day 21 of your cycle.

tips: Enter the first day of bleeding of your last period, not the day it ended.
If you are not sure of your cycle length, leave it at 28 days.
Pregnancy weeks are counted from your last period, about two weeks before conception, so at conception you are already "2 weeks pregnant".
If an early scan gives a date that differs by more than about a week, your clinic will usually go by the scan. Use the Ultrasound method to match it.
Milestone weeks differ a little between countries and clinics. Treat them as a guide and confirm with your care team.
problems: The calculator says the date is in the future
The last period or scan date must be today or earlier. Check the year in the date box.
My due date differs from my doctor's
Doctors often adjust the date after a dating scan, or use slightly different rules. Their date is the one to follow.
It says the pregnancy would be too long
The date you entered is too long ago, more than 44 weeks. Check that you entered this year, not last year.
The cycle length is not accepted
Enter a whole number from 20 to 45. Outside this range the period method is not reliable; an ultrasound gives a better estimate.
